knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The alert places systems above 5,600 bar litres per minute in Class B, which needs training and assessment through a registered training organisation [WSV-JET].
Every hose must be rated at or above the maximum operating pressure, so the defective hose is tagged out and replaced [WSV-JET].
An unknown nozzle has an unknown output. Its specification is confirmed against the manufacturer's data before use.

practicalCriteria: Identifies the class and maximum operating pressure of a sample machine from the manufacturer's data, and records them on an equipment register, with any value not in the data stated as not given.
Completes a pre-use inspection on a sample set (hoses, fittings, nozzle, guard, trigger, electrical lead and plug), and tags out a seeded fault.
Checks each hose and fitting rating against the sample machine's maximum operating pressure, and rejects any part rated lower.
passRule: Assessor review of the equipment register, the inspection record and the rating check on the sample set, with all three practical criteria met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Equipment register with class and maximum operating pressure from data
Pre-use inspection log and RCD test record
Tag-out record for the seeded fault
stopWorkCriteria: A hose or fitting is rated below the maximum operating pressure and is used
An unidentified nozzle or an unapproved modification is fitted
An RCD is missing or untested before electrical equipment is used near water
Equipment with a leak, cut hose or electrical fault is run
